title: The retrieval process: search, reranking and filters

videos.script: Ask for error E-4104, and the search returns the error table. Barely. {{vector}} To an embedding model, two error codes that differ in one digit are almost the same string. {{blind}} An older kind of search counts words. It finds the code at once, and misses a customer who says send back instead of return. {{lexical}} So you run both, and merge them by rank, because their scores cannot be compared. {{hybrid}} Then a slower model reads the question and each candidate together, and puts them in a better order. Sometimes. {{rerank}} Watch it move the price of express delivery from fifth place to second. Then watch it put last year's policy first. {{wrong}} No score can tell that a policy was replaced. That takes a filter. {{filter}} Last, the question nobody wants to ask. How good does a result have to be before you use it at all? {{threshold}} Every answer in this lesson is a number measured on the same questions. {{end}}
